title: DOE Selects 19 Critical-Minerals Processing Projects
summary: DOE announced more than $45.7 million for 19 selected projects intended to advance pilot-scale processing and recovery of critical materials, including magnesium and rare-earth elements.
key_findings: The announcement identifies 19 selected projects and more than $45.7 million in intended federal support.
DOE describes the work as pilot-scale processing and recovery development rather than commercial production.
The selected portfolio includes material-specific projects whose later evidence must be tracked through awards, project execution, facility records, validation, and production.
why_it_matters: The selections move the federal critical-minerals trail one stage downstream from an open funding opportunity, while leaving award execution, technical performance, scale, cost, and production unproven.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a dated selection-stage record to the Critical Minerals pathway.
Creates recipient and project lanes for later award, location, pilot, and production checks.
Supports comparison between program intent, selection, obligation, delivery, and operating capacity.
evidence_limits: A selection announcement is not necessarily a completed award or obligation.
Pilot-scale intent does not establish technical success, commercial economics, permitting, offtake, or production.
The announcement does not demonstrate reduced import reliance or resilient supply at system scale.
